cards.hearing: You may be hearing that gas and diesel prices are still high, and that it's even becoming a big topic in this year's elections.
cards.why: That matters at home because diesel moves the trucks that deliver groceries and goods, so higher fuel costs can show up later in the prices we pay at the store.
cards.but: But election years always bring a lot of noise about energy costs, and markets have lived through plenty of election cycles before.
cards.story: Think of a family road trip where gas prices spike for one stretch of highway. You don't cancel the whole vacation over one pricey fill-up, you just keep driving toward where you're headed.
say: We don't rewrite your plan because of one election-year headline.
Fuel costs come and go, but your long-term plan is built to handle that.

cards.hearing: You may be hearing that borrowing costs, like mortgage rates, ticked a little higher recently.
cards.why: That matters because when interest rates move up even slightly, it can mean a bit more cost to borrow for a house, a car, or a business loan.
cards.but: But small moves in interest rates happen often, and they don't change the shape of a long-term plan built for years, not weeks.
cards.story: Picture adjusting the thermostat by one degree. You'll notice it if you're paying close attention, but it's not a reason to redesign the whole house.
say: A small tick in rates doesn't mean we rethink your whole plan.
We watch rates, but we don't let one small move drive big decisions.

cards.hearing: You may be hearing that stocks have been fairly calm, drifting a little higher this week without any major news driving it.
cards.why: That matters because quiet weeks like this are often when long-term plans quietly do their job, without any drama to report.
cards.but: But calm weeks don't mean nothing is happening — they're actually part of how long-term growth is built, one steady stretch at a time.
cards.story: Think of a long hike where some days are just flat, easy trail. Nothing exciting happens, but you're still covering ground toward where you're going.
say: Quiet weeks are still progress, even when there's nothing to report.
We like boring weeks. They're usually the plan working as intended.
